business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Reverse Logistics and Returned Goods Quality Grading

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law foundation with customary land tenure overlay)

World Trade Organization membership and obligations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (No. 20 of 2007), as amended including the Money Laundering Prevention (Amendment) Act 2018; International Companies Act 1987 (No. 24 of 1987), as amended; Companies Act 2001; Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) AML/CFT Guidelines; Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Registered Agent licensing and Beneficial Ownership requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each proposed director, shareholder, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the issuing state is an Apostille Convention Contracting State) or Consular Legalization at the Samoan embassy, high commission, or honorary consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential and/or business address (recent utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or bank, with notarial certification in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate due diligence bundle for any corporate shareholder, including certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and register of directors and shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or competent company registry in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter regarding the beneficial owner's principal banking relationship

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, and relevant family members or close associates against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Samoa domestic sanctions notifications, and reputable global PEP databases such as World-Check or Dow Jones. Screening must be completed before incorporation engagement acceptance and repeated on a risk-sensitive basis during the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) International Companies Registry portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the working language of the Registry. The proposed name must be expressed in Roman/Latin alphabetical characters; Samoan diacritics are generally avoided. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and must end with a recognized corporate designator such as 'International Company', 'I.C.', 'Limited', or 'Ltd.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant through its licensed registered agent may file a written notice of appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 working days, annexing evidence of distinctiveness and compliance with the International Companies Act 1987. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may petition the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour for administrative review within 30 days. Court action is not available until administrative remedies are exhausted. Alternatively, a fresh reservation may be submitted using a different distinctive name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical statutory registered office in Samoa and the services of a licensed SIFA registered agent are mandatory. A virtual office may be used only as a non-statutory correspondence or back-office address and cannot replace the licensed registered agent's physical presence in Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 5% likelihood for unannounced inspection of the low-risk reverse-logistics operator's own premises, and approximately 20% likelihood for SIFA examination of the registered agent's client files and registered office.

Government incorporation filing fee for Samoa International Company

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Acts 2008, 2011 and 2024), ss. 4, 5, 14, 15 (incorporation procedure), s. 33 (registered office), s. 46 (directors), s. 105 (annual return); the domestic Companies Act 2006 does not apply to International Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia; registry services administered through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) licensed registered agents.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association submitted with Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation), Notice of Registered Office (IC-1A) and Notice of First Directors (IC-1B).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an International Company; capital may be unpaid at incorporation. No escrow, capital deposit or paid-up certificate is required. Authorised capital up to USD 1,000,000 attracts the US$150 fee; higher bands are separately rated and shares may be denominated in any convertible currency.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscribers hereby subscribe for and take up the initial 1,000 ordinary shares of USD 1.00 each allotted by the Company, and the Directors are authorised to issue share certificates accordingly. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office of the Company be fixed at the office of [Licensed Registered Agent], Apia, Samoa, and the Registrar of International Companies be notified accordingly. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [Name] be appointed as Director, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as authorised signatory, each holding office until removal or resignation. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the officers arrange all statutory filings, pay incorporation fees, appoint advisers, and open corporate bank accounts to conduct cross-border reverse logistics business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies via SIFA-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application stating the proposed name plus two alternatives. The name must end with 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Ltd' or similar and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing Samoa International Company or a reserved foreign name. Provide a short distinctiveness statement. The name is reserved for 30 days (renewable).
required_dossiers: Identification of ultimate beneficial owner (where available)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, file a written consent letter from the existing name holder or add a distinguishing word, then re-submit with fresh alternatives.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies (MCIL) filing counter, Apia; draft prepared by SIFA-licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English in statutory form. The Memorandum must state the company name, Samoan registered office (licensed agent's address), liability limited by shares, object clause covering cross-border reverse logistics, returned merchandise quality grading, warehousing and ancillary services, authorised capital (e.g., USD 1,000,000 divided into 1,000,000 ordinary shares) and any restrictions. The subscriber signs before a witness; the Articles may adopt standard Table A-style governance provisions.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered agent from licensed Samoa trustee or agent
Statement of non-resident ownership (if all shareholders are foreign)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries defective wording (e.g., improper share denomination or object clause), amend and re-execute the document within 14 days of the requisition; a second requisition attracts a US$25 re-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing, Fee Payment and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies (MCIL) / SIFA online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the executed Memorandum and Articles with Form IC-1, Notice of Registered Office, Notice of First Directors and director/secretary consents. Pay the statutory incorporation fee (US$150 for authorised capital up to USD 1,000,000; additional US$50 per further block) by bank transfer to the MCIL/SIFA account. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation with a unique company number.
required_dossiers: Consent forms of directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is held for verification beyond SLA, the licensed agent may file an expedite letter; the certificate, once issued, is dated retroactively to the date of the original filing upon cure of any defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office at the licensed agent's address in Apia. Appoint at least one director (natural person or corporate entity) and, if desired, a company secretary; non-resident directors and shareholders are permitted. Record the appointments in the Register of Directors and Register of Members maintained at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Register of Members and share ledger
Consent and appointment letters for each director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to file director changes within 21 days incurs a late penalty; remedy by filing an out-of-time notice accompanied by a board resolution confirming the overdue change and payment of the penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Exemption Confirmation and Annual Compliance Prerequisites
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); Ministry of Revenue (MOR) confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: An International Company is automatically exempt from Samoa income tax, stamp duty, transfer duty and capital gains tax on its non-Samoan sourced operations. Obtain the SIFA Certificate of Exemption confirming tax-exempt status. Maintain offshore economic substance or engage only in qualifying offshore business to preserve the exemption. File the annual return and pay the annual government fee (US$200) within 12 months of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is late, the company is liable to strike-off after 90 days; reinstate by filing all outstanding annual returns, paying arrears plus penalties, and obtaining a Registrar's restoration order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Payment Rails Configuration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ANZ Bank Samoa, Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa, or Airwallex
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate operating and multi-currency account. Present certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles, board resolution authorising signatories, directors' passport copies, ultimate beneficial owner declaration and the licensed agent's confirmation letter. Configure Local_ACH and Airwallex payment rails for cross-border settlement of returned-goods refunds and vendor payables. Standard KYC/AML due diligence applies at standard low-risk tier.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further source-of-funds evidence, provide notarised board resolutions and invoices; the licensed agent's endorsement letter can expedite final approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - Business Licensing Division / Samoa Business Registry; Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) for land use
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence under the Business Licences Act 1998 (mandatory only if a physical warehouse, grading facility or office is established in Samoa; wholly offshore International Companies remain exempt under the International Companies Act 1987)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Preliminary Environmental Assessment / Activity Registration under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 and EIA Regulations 2011; a full EIA Report is not triggered for non-hazardous returned-goods warehousing and grading, but is required if the facility stores e-waste, batteries, refrigerated units or hazardous substances.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Samoa National Environmental Standards (BOD5 ≤ 20 mg/L; TSS ≤ 30 mg/L) under the Water Resources Management Act 2008; segregation and disposal of packaging waste per the Waste Management Act 2011; no ozone-depleting substance emissions; export of rejected electronics and e-waste requires MNRE transboundary movement consent under the Basel Convention and the Ozone Layer Protection Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) for any warehouse or grading facility exceeding 200 m2; building approval and structural load certification under the Building Act 2014 issued by the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI); workplace registration, hazard management plan and first-aid inspections under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002 (MCIL); expatriate managers require MCIL Labour Division work permits and Samoa Immigration entry permits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue of the Independent State of Samoa (MfR); official taxpayer portal and e-services: revenue.gov.ws (Samoa Tax e-Services, including TIN registration, VAGST registration, and electronic return filing).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company first incorporates under the International Companies Act 1987 through a licensed registered agent in Samoa. The registered agent then files the MfR taxpayer application on the company's behalf, submitting the certificate of incorporation, IC registration certificate, registered office and agent details, and shareholder/director identification documents. The MfR issues a TIN that functions as the single administrative identifier for all tax interactions. Because the IC is a Tax_Exempt_Zone entity, the TIN supports VAGST filing, economic substance reporting, and Bank of Samoa exchange-control declarations rather than income tax assessment. If the IC separately makes taxable supplies into the Samoa domestic economy above the VAGST threshold, the agent or local representative must complete a supplementary VAGST registration through the MfR portal; otherwise, the IC remains administratively registered but not liable to domestic income tax or VAGST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or entity-classification election is available under Samoa law. A Samoa International Company is automatically and mandatorily classified as an offshore tax-exempt company under the International Companies Act 1987 and does not elect its classification. The only statutory elections are (i) voluntary VAGST registration to recover input credits where the IC carries on minor taxable activity, and (ii) an election to be treated as a non-resident IC for territorial and treaty purposes, subject to MfR approval. Samoa does not recognise hybrid-mismatch or disregarded-entity elections; reliance on foreign pass-through characterisation must be substantiated by a Samoa tax ruling from the Ministry of Revenue.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (i.e., SAT 100,000) of taxable supplies in a rolling 12-month period; compulsory registration for exceeding suppliers and voluntary registration permitted below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or continuous-control mandate is in force in Samoa. Samoa has not implemented CTC e-invoicing, digital stamping, SAF-T, or API-based transactional clearance. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue prescribed tax invoices and simplified retail receipts, file periodic VAGST returns via the MfR online e-Services portal, and retain all electronic and paper records for the statutory seven-year period. Large taxpayers are required to file electronically under the Tax Administration Act 2019, but no third-party invoice clearance or digital stamping is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2003, goods qualify for 0% output tax only where they are physically exported from Samoa, normally within 28 days of supply, under a Customs export declaration, and are not supplied for local consumption in Samoa. Services qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is a non-resident located outside Samoa at the time of supply and the services are not performed for local persons or directly connected with real property in Samoa. Reverse-logistics services (inspection, quality grading, light repair, repackaging, and warehousing of returned merchandise) are zero-rated only when performed for an offshore principal under a documented return-merchandise chain, paid for offshore, and evidenced by export documentation; any local release or resale of remediated goods in Samoa is a taxable supply at 15% VAGST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa Customs Service) or electronic export permit evidencing physical departure of goods from Samoa
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the ocean/air carrier confirming export and destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (Central Bank of Samoa or licensed commercial bank) evidencing timely repatriation of the offshore sale proceeds
Commercial invoice, packing list, and freight and insurance documents matching the export declaration
Return-Merchandise Authorization (RMA) and service contract evidencing the offshore principal's ownership of the returned goods and the reverse-logistics service chain
Warehouse inventory, grading, and disposal records linking each unit of goods to the zero-rated supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to post-export audit by the Ministry of Revenue against the customs and FX documentation bundle. If the export is fictitious, the goods are diverted into the domestic market, or export proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day window, the MfR will claw back the refunded VAGST with statutory interest, impose tax shortfall penalties up to 150% of the avoided tax for intentional concealment or fraud, and may initiate criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment for fraudulent VAGST refund claims. For a Samoa International Company, a failed export or exemption audit also triggers the Samoa International Financial Authority economic-substance review and may result in revocation of the IC's Tax_Exempt_Zone status and retrospective reassessment as a domestic taxable entity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tala (WST) is convertible for current account transactions, including trade-related payments, dividends, and service fees, under a liberalised exchange control regime administered by the Central Bank of Samoa. Capital account transactions require case-by-case approval, and profit remittances are permitted subject to submission of audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and evidence of foreign direct investment registration. Non-resident International Companies enjoy statutory tax exemption but remain subject to exchange control reporting thresholds for inward and outward transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to Samoa within 180 days from the date of shipment or export. International Companies operating under the International Companies Act are not generally subject to mandatory conversion of export receipts into WST; proceeds may be retained in foreign currency in designated external accounts, provided that the Central Bank of Samoa is notified and documentary evidence of the underlying export transaction is maintained. Any conversion to WST for local disbursement must be executed through an authorised dealer bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Airwallex and similar offshore fintech/EMI platforms are permitted for cross-border receipt and disbursement routing, but they are not licensed as deposit-taking institutions in Samoa. International Companies may use such platforms for trade settlement and reverse logistics disbursements, provided that (i) the underlying funds are not sourced from prohibited activity, (ii) the platform maintains an anti-money-laundering (AML) framework acceptable to the Central Bank of Samoa, and (iii) the Samoan entity maintains a local operational account for statutory reporting and tax clearance interactions. The use of EMIs is legally constrained to non-resident business accounts and cannot be used as a substitute for a Samoan bank account where exchange control declaration is required for inbound capital injections or profit remittances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not required to appear physically before a Samoan bank for standard operational account opening, provided that the bank accepts certified true copies of identification documents and notarised corporate resolutions. However, physical attendance or a video-conference interview may be mandated by the bank's AML/KYC officer where a director is a politically exposed person (PEP), where the beneficial ownership structure involves trusts or nominee shareholders, or where the account is designated as high-risk due to unusual transaction patterns. Remote opening is permitted for International Companies, subject to a minimum due diligence period and the submission of company registry excerpts, trust deeds, and source of funds declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity involving a Samoan international trust or nominee shareholder arrangement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified deed of trust, trust register extract, AML beneficial ownership declaration naming each natural person settlor and beneficiary, sworn statutory declaration by the resident agent, corporate registry certificate of good standing, and bank reference letters for all economic owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for reverse logistics working capital derived from cross-border e-commerce settlement platforms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform transaction statements covering at least 12 months, marketplace settlement reports, signed customer contracts, customs/import records evidencing returned goods flows, invoice and packing list bundles, and a written medium-risk assessment memo from the bank's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume or fragmented inbound wire transfers inconsistent with stated revenue profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed cash flow forecast model, board-approved treasury policy, underlying trade agreements with global merchants, refund obligation schedule and reverse logistics performance records, tax clearance certificates, and monthly compliance pack addressed to the bank's AML/KYC unit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from non-resident shareholders or related group entities must be routed through the Samoan banking system via SWIFT MT103, MT202, or MT210 messages, using the appropriate Harmonised System / balance-of-payments purpose codes. For International Companies, the recommended inbound purpose code is 'Other External Assets / Foreign Direct Investment – Equity Investment' for share capital injections and 'Cross-border Trade-related Working Capital' for intercompany loans. The Central Bank of Samoa imposes a notification obligation on authorised dealer banks for all inbound foreign currency transfers exceeding WST 100,000, and the receiving bank must verify the corporate registry excerpt, director resolution, and underlying business plan before crediting a Capital Escrow Account. Proceeds of capital injections may be credited to a foreign currency denominated external account, converted to WST only through an authorised dealer, or held in escrow pending issuance of the International Company certificate from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for returned goods quality grading, refurbishment, carrier settlement, and refunds shall be cleared through the following rails: (i) local and regional supplier payments via Samoa ACH / FAST Settlement network where the beneficiary holds a Samoan account; (ii) cross-border supplier and logistics payments via SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers, MT202 cover payments for interbank reimbursements, and MT199 ancillary messages for reconciliation; (iii) commercial letters of credit using ICC UCP 600 rules where the counterparty requires documentary assurance; and (iv) bulk merchandising refunds and e-commerce payouts via Airwallex or equivalent licensed fintech credits routed to overseas bank accounts. All outbound transfers above WST 50,000 require the executing bank to submit an exchange control form to the Central Bank of Samoa; supporting documents include supplier contracts, customs declarations, and certificates of inspection for returned merchandise.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts with Authorised Dealer banks for WST/USD and WST/AUD, permitted for hedgers with a demonstrable commercial trade exposure arising from reverse logistics cross-border settlements

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing WST, permitted for settlement in USD or major convertible currencies where the counterparty is licensed in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction and the hedge is evidenced by underlying foreign-exchange exposure
Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST) for intercompany capital preservation purposes, subject to Central Bank notification when notional principal exceeds WST 1 million
Plain-vanilla FX swap deposits and spot-market layering, permitted for managing temporary liquidity mismatches between inbound refund settlements and disbursement cycles

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Renewal Fee (government license renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually on the incorporation anniversary; payment is due before the anniversary date, with a 60-day grace period under the International Companies Act 2015
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee (USD 50) accrues immediately after the grace period; continued non-payment for three months after the anniversary permits the Registrar to issue a notice of proposed strike-off; failure to remedy within 6-12 months leads to administrative deregistration and dissolution of the International Company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (statutory confirmation of company particulars, registered office, registered agent, directors, and shareholders)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due simultaneously with the annual renewal fee on the incorporation anniversary; the Registrar permits lodgment within the 60-day grace period without additional substantive penalty
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing within the grace period invalidates the company's good-standing certificate, triggers late penalty accruals, and constitutes a distinct default ground for the Registrar's administrative strike-off after 6-12 months of continued non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Verification Acknowledgement (annual confirmation embedded in the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the incorporation anniversary; the underlying register of registrable persons must be maintained at the registered office and updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Knowingly false or incomplete beneficial ownership information attracts statutory fines and director liability; continuing breach of the beneficial ownership provisions in the International Companies Act 2015 may be prosecuted separately from the fee default and supports strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Confirmation (annual standing declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmed in the Annual Return at each incorporation anniversary; any change of registered office or licensed registered agent must be lodged with the Registrar within 14 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or notify a licensed Samoa registered agent and registered office is a continuing statutory offence; the Registrar may strike off the company after issuing a formal warning notice if no agent is retained for three consecutive months

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not applicable: Samoa International Companies are statutorily exempt from mandatory independent audits under the International Companies Act 2015. An audit becomes compulsory only when required by the company's constituent documents, a shareholder resolution, a licensed lender or investor condition, or the consolidated audit rules of the beneficial owner's home jurisdiction (e.g., US GAAP group reporting).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act 2015 (accounting records provisions): the IC must keep books and records sufficient to accurately explain transactions, financial position, and to enable financial statements to be prepared. No mandatory IFRS or local GAAP election is imposed on International Companies; IFRS, US GAAP, or simplified modified-Cash/GAAP packages are commonly adopted for cross-border reverse logistics and returned-goods grading operations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the International Companies Act 2015 (as amended), every Samoa International Company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register at its registered office identifying registrable persons. No separate annual UBO return is filed; annual confirmation is effected through the Annual Return and renewal statement delivered to the Registrar on the anniversary. Registrable persons must be identified, verified, and their consent recorded; any acquisition or disposal of a beneficial interest, or a share transfer resulting in a change of registrable persons, must be reflected in the register within 30 days. Share warrants and bearer instrument mechanisms are prohibited for International Companies, and nominee arrangements must always disclose the underlying beneficial owner to the registered agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and Capital
Minute Book (directors' and members' minutes and written resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 650 - 1,500 per annum (typical Samoa licensed registered agent and registered office service fee; excludes Registrar disbursements and out-of-pocket expenses)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Statutory audit not required for WS_IC; voluntary certified audit or US GAAP review for investor or lender purposes typically ranges from USD 3,500 - 8,500 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (Samoa International Company holds a statutory Tax Exemption Certificate; no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or gift duty is imposed on exempt international companies under the International Companies Act 1987, s.208, as amended)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from income tax, withholding tax, and stamp duty for International Companies holding a valid Tax Exemption Certificate issued by the Samoa Ministry of Revenue; the exemption is generally granted for a period of up to 25 years from the date of incorporation and is renewable; no payroll tax or social security levy applies to expatriate non-resident personnel in reverse logistics operations conducted outside Samoa; no gross receipts tax applies to international shipping or transit-related services under the Tax Exemption Certificate

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return of International Company (Form IC-AR), filed with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) via the Samoa Companies Electronic Registration Portal; a separate Tax Exemption Certificate (Form TEC-1) and annual Certificate of Compliance application are lodged with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue and the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) respectively
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 28 days of the anniversary of incorporation; if the Tax Exemption Certificate has lapsed or been revoked, a Samoa Income Tax Return (Form IT-1) must be filed within 120 days after the fiscal year-end (fiscal year-end is 31 December unless a substituted accounting period is approved by the Commissioner of Revenue)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 - Company Name and Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the International Company exactly as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation, followed by the unique WS registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the English name; no translation or local trade name is required for exempt offshore status

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 - Date of Incorporation and Registered Office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date of incorporation and the physical registered-office address in Samoa maintained by a licensed registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Samoan street address is mandatory; a P.O. Box alone is not acceptable for the registered office field

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and licence number of the Samoan licensed international company registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must be a licensed International Company Agent registered under the International Companies Act 1987

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 - Share Capital and Share Classes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised and issued share capital, par value, and classes of shares (ordinary, preference, redeemable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital requirement; non-resident beneficial ownership is permitted and is not required to be disclosed in the public annual return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, nationalities, and residential addresses of all directors and registered shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and shareholders are permitted; only the registered shareholder names are filed, not the ultimate beneficial owner unless requested by SIFA under AML/CFT

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certificate number, issue date, and expiry date of the current Samoa Tax Exemption Certificate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a copy of the certificate; a lapsed certificate changes the entity from 0% to the standard filer status

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 - Declaration of Local Business Activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the International Company has not carried on commercial activity in Samoa, other than the exempt offshore activities permitted under the International Companies Act 1987
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reverse logistics screening, quality grading, and re-routing conducted wholly outside Samoa must be declared as offshore activity; any physical warehousing in Samoa may require standard corporate tax registration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of payment of the annual government fee and the SIFA Certificate of Compliance fee
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Evidence of wire payment via Local ACH or Airwallex to the MCIL consolidated fund is acceptable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 100 per month or part month up to a maximum of WST 1,000 per delayed return, plus a flat non-compliance surcharge of WST 200; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers automatic strike-off from the Register, forfeiture of assets to the Crown, and revocation of the Tax Exemption Certificate; late payment of the annual government fee accrues interest at 5% per annum

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Samoa does not impose dividend withholding tax; dividends paid by a tax-exempt International Company to its non-resident shareholders are wholly outside the Samoa Income Tax Act 2012 and may be remitted without deduction or prior approval
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Although the statutory rate is nil and treaty relief is therefore generally unnecessary for dividends, a non-resident payee claiming a reduced rate on royalties or interest must submit Form R-1 (Application for Treaty Relief) together with a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue; the TRC must be dated within 12 months of the payment date and accompanied by a beneficial-ownership declaration; Samoa's comprehensive Double Taxation Agreements (New Zealand, Australia, China, and Norway, supplemented by the OECD MLI) provide reduced rates of 0% to 10%; the Samoa Ministry of Revenue issues a Treaty Relief Confirmation Letter which the payor must retain for seven years
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest withholding tax rate is 15% and statutory royalty withholding tax rate is 15% for payments to non-residents; under the Samoa-New Zealand DTA, interest is limited to 10% and royalties to 10%; under the Samoa-China DTA, interest and royalties are each limited to 10%; payments made by a tax-exempt International Company to non-residents are not subject to Samoan withholding tax, but the payer must still apply the 0% exemption code and maintain a domestic withholding tax declaration from the recipient to document the exemption

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa does not prescribe a statutory currency threshold for Local File or Master File documentation for exempt International Companies; as an OECD Inclusive Framework member, Samoa follows the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines 2022. A Local File is recommended where connected-party cross-border transactions of the reverse logistics company exceed WST 1,000,000 per annum; a Master File is recommended where the group global turnover exceeds WST 5,000,000 and group-wide related-party transactions are present; the Tax Exemption Certificate does not exempt the entity from contemporaneous documentation obligations in the reverse logistics value chain
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not apply the European Union-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the International Companies Act 1987 ss.10, 25 and 213 impose a functional substance requirement: the company must maintain a registered office in Samoa, engage a licensed resident agent, and keep accounting records and registers at the agent's premises. For return merchandise and reverse logistics activities, the Samoa Ministry of Revenue and SIFA require evidence of real economic presence commensurate with the digital or physical flow of goods, including documented contracts, employee or director activity, third-party logistics agreements, and revenue records showing that the company is not a bare conduit; failure to demonstrate substance to the satisfaction of the Commissioner permits reclassification of the entity as a standard resident taxpayer and withdrawal of the Tax Exemption Certificate

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly submitting false particulars in the annual return, misrepresenting the volume of returned goods revenue, or operating Samoan warehousing and re-shipping activity while declaring zero local activity on the exempt international company return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 14 years under the Income Tax Act 2012 ss.110-112; reassessment of all profits at the standard corporate income tax rate of 27%; revocation of the Tax Exemption Certificate and a civil penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the reassessed tax, penalties, and interest; the Commissioner may obtain a personal recovery order, impose a travel ban, and seek disqualification of directors from managing any Samoan or international company for up to 10 years; criminal conviction leads to imprisonment and forfeiture of personal assets under the Proceeds of Crime Act

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and Sham Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the reverse logistics company as a pure invoice conduit with no registered office, no licensed agent, no accounting records, and no business purpose, while diverting profits from a connected foreign e-commerce or freight group through the Samoan entity solely to exploit the 0% tax exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off from the Register, cancellation of the Certificate of Compliance, and a default assessment equal to 25% of the gross remittances passing through the entity; the Tax Exemption Certificate is annulled retroactively and all protected years become taxable
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the entity is found to be a sham; directors and shadow directors are personally assessed for the corporate tax debt, compelled to make civil restitution of diverted profits, and may be subjected to asset freezing orders and travel bans pending full settlement

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file suspicious transaction reports with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit, refusing to provide beneficial ownership information to SIFA, or using the reverse logistics payments rail to launder proceeds from returned-goods fraud or customs duty evasion in a foreign jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of up to WST 250,000 per contravention under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2018; revocation of the registered agent's licence; the company's bank accounts with local ACH or Airwallex payment providers may be frozen; criminal prosecution carries fines of WST 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners face personal imposition of the monetary penalties where the AML breach was reckless; a personal travel ban and confiscation of assets can be ordered; directors of a licensed trust or company management provider are subject to permanent disqualification from the Samoa financial services industry

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing and Unauthorised Trading After Strike-Off
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to receive reverse logistics fees and repatriating profits after the annual return has been overdue for more than six months, after the company has been struck off the Register, or after the Tax Exemption Certificate has lapsed without a replacement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic dissolution and forfeiture of all company assets to the Samoan Crown; the company is treated as a standard resident taxpayer and assessed at 27% on all income earned during the default period; late filing penalties accrue at WST 100 per month and a WST 200 flat penalty per unfiled return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for debts incurred after the company was struck off; the court may order the directors to restore the company at their personal cost, pay the tax assessment from personal funds, and impose a prohibition on leaving Samoa until the outstanding penalties are settled
